subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw keep `timeoutSeconds` as the hard maximum run budget and add a separate activity/idle timeout, or should `timeoutSeconds` itself become activity-aware?
rationale: Both directions are technically possible, but the choice changes core runtime semantics, config schema, resource ceilings, upgrade behavior, and how the open partial timeout PRs should be reviewed.

options.title: Add idle timeout plus hard cap
options.body: Keep `timeoutSeconds` or a successor as the hard ceiling while adding an explicit liveness/idle budget so productive tool-heavy runs can continue without removing runaway protection.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Leave the existing hard timeout contract intact and focus on user-visible timeout notices, progress previews, and per-surface mitigations.

options.title: Narrow to existing PR slices
options.body: Review the open timeout-notice, Telegram-progress, and subagent-heartbeat PRs separately and defer the broader core timeout contract.

recommendation.title: Add idle timeout plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Keep `timeoutSeconds` or a successor as the hard ceiling while adding an explicit liveness/idle budget so productive tool-heavy runs can continue without removing runaway protection.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the shared agent timeout resolver and gateway abort semantics that Peter Steinberger introduced and previously refactored.
